assumptions: Every token count follows research/scripts/h1_cost.py: pi's own estimate, characters over four, and the high estimate counts three characters per token (token_scale 4/3) on input and output alike.

Measured shapes come from the committed results named in inputs, each checked against its sha256 in research/results/MANIFEST.md; a run marked estimated from the design takes its shape from design_shapes or from the nearest measured condition, as its count says.

Reasoning output tokens per call of the model under test, where pi-ai sends an off it honours: 0 (low) and 1,024 (high); where off is ignored: 256 and 4,096 (research/configs/h1-cost.json). Which applies is the pi-ai catalogue's flag in research/results/h1-cost.json. Judges and simulators reason not at all.
GateMem's judge makes one to three attempts per session (upstream's retries); LongMemEval's one call per session.

No prompt caching, batch discount or provider minimum; HTTP retries are not counted; prices are OpenRouter's list prices on the day fetched (research/configs/openrouter-prices.json), and the pi-ai 1.3.0 catalogue's (2026-10-15) are given for the totals beside them.
A row marked shared_with makes no new call under rule 7 (a re-run with the same cells is a cache hit) and enters no total, except where an option of item 2 makes it new.
The ceiling per run is ceiling_factor times its high estimate (card RV1, lead-decisions item 3a).

exclude.why: item 24: H4 runs on GateMem only
item 20: the store family leaves H4's equivalence test (ADR 0035); the mem0 arm and the model and condition arms stay
item 25: C7's test is dropped, C7 equals C5 in benchmark sessions

mab-question.basis: one read and one answer as on GateMem: two calls, a 300-token prompt and a top-20 read of context chunks, 256 tokens a chunk (low); four calls (two more reads) and 1,024 tokens a chunk (high), input (r + 1) prompt + (8 + read) r (r + 1) / 2 as research/scripts/h1_cost.py counts it

merit-episode.basis: MERIT's paper (docs/readings/litreview/2609.05441-merit.md): about 0.00046 dollars per D1-easy episode under no memory on gpt-4.1-mini, about 1,000 input tokens; the low takes 3 calls and 1,500 tokens, the high 8 calls and ten times the tokens

merit-episode-c1.basis: MERIT's full replay, 2.7 to 3.9 times the per-episode cost of the best memory (the paper, Sec. 5.6); the low takes about 2.7 times merit-episode's input

tau2-agent-episode.basis: tau2's agent: 8 calls of about 5,000 input tokens (the domain policy, the tool schemas and the dialogue) and 100 output (low); 20 calls of 12,000 and 300 (high)

tau2-induction.basis: Agent Workflow Memory (ADR 0012): one induction call per recorded trajectory, the trajectory in and the workflows out

tau2-retail-judge.basis: one call per retail episode for its natural-language assertions

tau2-user-episode.basis: tau2's LLM user simulator answers every agent turn: 8 calls of 1,500 input and 60 output (low), 20 calls of 5,000 and 150 (high)

name: cost-table

options.item_1_note: Item 1's option (b) names only M1; the other two models keep their makers and take the other two roles. Option (c) names no small model; gpt-6-luna and mistral-small-2603 bound the range item 1 quotes, with M2 and M3 as in (a).

item_2.a: H1 runs its 728 utility checkpoints (MGS), and H2's GateMem C2 and C5 at medium reuse every H1 cell
item_2.b: H1 drops its utility checkpoints; H2 still needs them for U, so its C2 and C5 utility cells at medium become new calls

item_47.a: decided with the spend: priced as registered (c)

b.text: a seeded 250-question subset by amendment: calls in proportion to the questions, 0.5 of the full run (the L4 review's table gives about 47,600)

openrouter-prices.source: OpenRouter's public model list, https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (no key), each model's pricing.prompt, pricing.completion and pricing.input_cache_read, in dollars per token, multiplied here by one million
